questions.question: The system equation is written first because:
options: It is the only equation in which the unknown tension does not appear
It avoids having to use Newton's second law
The total mass is always easier to measure

options: Drawing a separate free-body diagram for each body
Choosing the body with fewest forces for step two
Stating a positive direction before writing equations
Writing "50 + T = 10a" — putting the tension into the system equation

subtopics.title: Over the Pulley — Table Edge and Incline

questions.question: A 4 kg block (μk = 0,25) on a table is joined over a pulley to a 6 kg hanging mass. The acceleration is:
The tension in that string is:
The tension is LESS than the hanging weight because:
options: The pulley absorbs some of the force
If the tension equalled the weight there would be no net force and no downward acceleration
Friction on the table reduces the tension

questions.question: A 6 kg block on a frictionless 30° incline is joined over a pulley to a 9 kg hanging mass. The force opposing the motion in the system equation is:
options: 29,4 N, the component mg sinθ of the block's weight

questions.question: Two trolleys joined by a rope share one acceleration because:
options: The rope cannot stretch, so they move together
Friction is the same on both

questions.question: When you treat the two trolleys as one object, the rope tension:
options: Must be added to the push
Cancels out, because it pulls the two trolleys in opposite directions

questions.question: When drawing the rope's force on a trolley, the arrow points:
options: Along the rope, away from that trolley towards the other one, because a rope can only pull
Into the trolley, because ropes push when tight
In whichever direction makes the answer positive

questions.question: In move one of the recipe you should:
options: Add the masses, add only the outside forces, and leave the rope out
Use only the heavier body's mass

questions.question: In move two you should choose:
options: The heavier body, because it carries more force
Whichever body the question names first
The body with the fewest forces acting on it

questions.question: Using the friction of BOTH crates in the small crate's own equation would:
options: Make no difference to the answer
Only affect the acceleration, not the tension
Be correct, since the crates are connected
Be wrong — every quantity in a single-body equation must belong to that body alone

options: They are perpendicular to the motion and cancel each other
They are too small to matter
They are already included in the tension

questions.question: A string holds a falling 6 kg mass with 29,4 N while the mass weighs 58,8 N. This tells you:
options: The mass is accelerating downward, so the tension must be less than the weight
